learning.learning_goal: Understand that 'how many more' asks how many items are left after two groups are paired.
learning.big_idea: Pair one item from each group. Count what is left in the larger group.

screens.label: Lesson 001
screens.title: How many more?
screens.body: Put two groups side by side. Pair one item in the first group with one item in the second group. Count the items left without partners. That number tells how many more.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: What does “how many more” ask us to find?
screens.prompt: Ava has 14 stickers. Luis has 8. How many more stickers does Ava have?

choices.text: 6, because 6 of Ava’s stickers have no partner
choices.feedback: Pair Luis’s 8 stickers with 8 of Ava’s 14 stickers. Ava has 6 stickers left, so she has 6 more.

hints: Pair Luis’s 8 stickers with 8 of Ava’s stickers. Do not put both groups into one total.
After making 8 pairs, Ava has 6 stickers left without partners. Count those 6 stickers.

screens.label: Observe
screens.title: Pair the blocks in the two rows.

visual.message: Each bottom block is directly below a top block. Those blocks are partners. The top row still has blocks left.

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What do the glowing blocks show?

visual.message: The glowing blocks have no partner in the bottom row. Count them to find how many more blocks are in the top row.

choices.text: How many blocks are left after pairing
choices.feedback: Correct. Pair the first 9 top blocks with the 9 bottom blocks. The 6 glowing blocks are left without partners, so the top row has 6 more.

hints: Start at the left. Give each bottom block one partner from the top row.
Nine pairs can be made. The glowing top blocks do not have partners.
Count the 6 glowing blocks. They tell how many more are in the top row.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: What does “how many more” mean?

visual.message: First pair the two groups. Then count what is left in the larger group.

screens.phraseMeaning: Pair the groups. Count what is left.
screens.guidance: “In all” or “altogether” asks you to join the groups. “How many more” asks you to pair the groups and count what is left in the larger group.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Pair. Count what is left.
screens.hook: Larger number − smaller number = how many are left
screens.body: The minus sign (−) means subtract. Here, subtraction counts the items left after the two groups are paired.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which number sentence counts what is left?

visual.message: There are 15 top blocks and 9 bottom blocks. Pair 9 from each row. Which number sentence finds the top blocks left over?

choices.feedback: Correct. Start with the 15 top blocks. Subtract the 9 blocks that received partners. Six top blocks are left.

hints: Start with all 15 top blocks. Nine of them receive partners from the bottom row.
Subtract the 9 paired blocks from the 15 top blocks: 15 − 9.

visual.message: Fifteen top blocks minus the 9 paired blocks leaves 6 unpaired blocks.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: How many top shells are left without partners?

visual.message: Pair 7 top shells with the 7 bottom shells. The glowing top shells are left without partners.

choices.feedback: Correct. Seven pairs use 7 of the 11 top shells. Four top shells are left, so 11 is 4 more than 7.

hints: Start on the left. Pair each of the 7 bottom shells with one top shell.
Seven of the 11 top shells have partners. Count the 4 glowing shells that are left.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: Nia read 16 pages. Theo read 9 pages. How many more pages did Nia read?
hints: Imagine 16 marks for Nia’s pages and 9 marks for Theo’s pages. Pair 9 marks from each group.
Seven of Nia’s marks are left without partners. You can also calculate 16 − 9 = 7.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: What should you remember?
screens.prompt: When a problem asks “how many more,” what should you do?

choices.text: Pair the groups and count what is left
choices.feedback: Correct. Pair one item from each group. The items left in the larger group tell how many more.

hints: Do not join both groups. Put them side by side and make pairs.
After pairing, count the items left in the larger group.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea in a new setting.
screens.prompt: A blue notebook costs $18 and a red notebook costs $11. How much more does the blue notebook cost?

choices.feedback: $18 − $11 = $7, so the blue notebook costs $7 more.

hints: Pair $11 of the blue notebook’s $18 cost with the red notebook’s $11 cost.
$7 of the blue notebook’s cost is left. You can calculate this as $18 − $11 = $7.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What did you discover?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains the idea.

choices.text: Subtraction can count what is left after two groups are paired.
The word more always means add.

hints: The blocks were paired one for one. The glowing blocks were left without partners.
The subtraction sentence counted the blocks left after pairing.

screens.title: You found how many more.
screens.body: You paired two groups, counted what was left, and used subtraction to show the same action.
